resource.name: aws_cloudwatch_log_group
resource.description: Provides a CloudWatch Log Group resource.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of Amazon CloudWatch Log Groups, providing a centralized solution for aggregating, storing, and organizing application and system logs. Common use cases include setting up log retention policies, monitoring application performance, and integrating logs with CloudWatch metrics or alarms for real-time insights. Users can configure key settings such as log retention periods, encryption with KMS keys, and resource lifecycle rules to optimize log storage and security.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates basic configuration of the `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` resource, including setting a custom log group name (`name`) and applying tags (`tags`) to organize resources by environment and application. Useful for users looking to create and tag CloudWatch log groups for structured resource management."

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument in the `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` resource represents the unique identifier of the log group, typically auto-generated by AWS upon creation. While not required to be explicitly set by the user, it can be used to reference or manage the log group programmatically, enabling workflows that depend on identifying specific log groups for monitoring, retention, or access control purposes.

arguments.name: kms_key_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN of the KMS Key to use when encrypting log data. Please note, after the AWS KMS CMK is disassociated from the log group, AWS CloudWatch Logs stops encrypting newly ingested data for the log group. All previously ingested data remains encrypted, and AWS CloudWatch Logs requires permissions for the CMK whenever the encrypted data is requested.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_id` argument allows users to specify the ARN of an AWS KMS Key for encrypting log data within the `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` resource. By setting this argument, users can enforce encryption for newly ingested log data, aligning with security and compliance requirements, while ensuring previously ingested data remains encrypted and accessible with the specified KMS Key.

arguments.name: log_group_class
arguments.description: (Optional) Specified the log class of the log group. Possible values are: `STANDARD` or `INFREQUENT_ACCESS`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `log_group_class` argument for the `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` resource allows users to specify the storage tier for the log group, choosing between `STANDARD` for regular access or `INFREQUENT_ACCESS` for cost-optimized storage of less frequently accessed logs. This configuration helps users manage log storage costs and access patterns based on their application's logging needs.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Optional, Forces new resource) The name of the log group. If omitted, Terraform will assign a random, unique name.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument for the `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` resource allows users to define a custom, human-readable identifier for the log group, enabling better organization and management of log streams within AWS CloudWatch. If omitted, Terraform generates a unique name automatically, but specifying this argument is useful for aligning log group names with application environments, workflows, or naming conventions.

arguments.name: name_prefix
arguments.description: (Optional, Forces new resource) Creates a unique name beginning with the specified prefix. Conflicts with `name`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name_prefix` argument for the `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` resource allows users to define a unique name for the log group that begins with a specified prefix, enabling dynamic naming patterns often used for environments, projects, or automated workflows. Setting this argument helps users manage naming conventions and avoid conflicts, particularly in scenarios where multiple log groups are created programmatically or need to adhere to a specific naming structure.

arguments.name: retention_in_days
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies the number of days you want to retain log events in the specified log group. Possible values are: 1, 3, 5, 7, 14, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, 365, 400, 545, 731, 1096, 1827, 2192, 2557, 2922, 3288, 3653, and 0. If you select 0, the events in the log group are always retained and never expire.
arguments.llm_summary: The `retention_in_days` argument for the `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` resource allows users to define the lifecycle of log events by specifying the number of days logs are retained before being automatically deleted. Setting this argument helps manage storage costs and compliance requirements by controlling log retention periods, with the option to retain logs indefinitely by specifying `0`.

arguments.name: skip_destroy
arguments.description: (Optional) Set to true if you do not wish the log group (and any logs it may contain) to be deleted at destroy time, and instead just remove the log group from the Terraform state.
arguments.llm_summary: The `skip_destroy` argument in the `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` resource allows users to control the lifecycle behavior of the log group during resource destruction. When set to `true`, it prevents the deletion of the log group and its logs, ensuring data retention while removing the resource from Terraform's state—ideal for scenarios requiring log preservation beyond the Terraform-managed lifecycle.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the resource. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` resource allows users to assign key-value metadata to the log group, enabling organization, categorization, and resource management based on tags such as environment, cost center, or application. Configuring this argument helps streamline governance, billing, and search functionality by associating the log group with meaningful identifiers, and it can override provider-level default tags for enhanced customization.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are applied to the log group for organizational, management, or cost allocation purposes. By setting this argument, users can ensure consistent tagging across resources, enabling streamlined resource tracking, billing analysis, and compliance with tagging policies.

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) specifying the log group. Any `:*` suffix added by the API, denoting all CloudWatch Log Streams under the CloudWatch Log Group, is removed for greater compatibility with other AWS services that do not accept the suffix.
